Why Spreadsheets Still Dominate Accounting Workflows
Even with sophisticated systems in place, almost all organizations report the same issue.
, 90% of organizations still rely on outdated spreadsheets and manual forms for some of their most vital business data.
If a process is not handled directly in the ERP, it likely happens in Excel, whether it is mapping accounts, reconciling intercompany entries, or tracking audit adjustments.
The impact of manual work is significant. Routine processes create bottlenecks that eat up valuable time. A
found that finance teams spend nearly one-third of their time on reconciliation alone.

Even at high-performing companies, analysts dedicate 40% of their efforts to collecting data rather than interpreting it. This leaves little room for strategic analysis and keeps teams operating reactively instead of proactively.
The spreadsheet is still the biggest competitor to accounting automation. It is also the biggest opportunity for transformation.
